notes: Controller checks run before dependent bus, signal, and device checks.
Bus checks establish transport readiness before attached-device probes.
Part smoke-test metadata is reused for device-level validation checks.
ESP32-S3FN8 based module used as the controller core on M5Stack Dial

checks.description: Confirm the connected unit reports or probes as the configured controller module and MCU family.
checks.passCriteria: The matched unit identity agrees with the configured module or MCU family.

checks.description: Confirm the controller transport required for validation is present and usable.
checks.passCriteria: A transport such as serial, USB-serial/JTAG, or STLink VCP is available for the selected unit.

checks.description: Confirm the controller exposes the declared UART capability needed by the board config.
Confirm the controller exposes the declared I2C capability needed by the board config.
Confirm the controller exposes the declared SPI capability needed by the board config.
Confirm the controller exposes the declared I2S capability needed by the board config.
Confirm the controller exposes the declared TWAI capability needed by the board config.
Confirm the controller exposes the declared USB capability needed by the board config.
Confirm the controller exposes the declared ADC capability needed by the board config.
Confirm the controller exposes the declared PWM capability needed by the board config.
Confirm signal power_hold can be driven to the configured state for board bring-up.
checks.passCriteria: The signal can be driven to the requested board-level state.

checks.description: Confirm bus internal_i2c is configured on the declared controller peripheral and signal lines.
checks.passCriteria: The bus can be opened using the declared controller peripheral and line mapping.

checks.description: Scan the internal_i2c bus and compare observed addresses against the board config.
checks.passCriteria: All configured addresses are observed or any missing and unexpected addresses are reported explicitly.
failureNotes: Missing configured addresses indicate that a declared device is absent, unpowered, or misconfigured.
Unexpected addresses should be reported as observed-but-undeclared devices, not silently ignored.

notes: An I2C bus must be configured before probing the device.
Any board-level wake or power-hold wiring should already be stable.

checks.description: Confirm device rtc is reachable through its declared I2C path.
checks.passCriteria: The device acknowledges on I2C and returns readable register data.
failureNotes: A missing ACK usually indicates the bus is not powered or the address is wrong.
Readable but invalid time data should be treated as present but unconfigured.

checks.description: Probe the configured I2C address and confirm an ACK is received.
checks.passCriteria: The device acknowledges on I2C and returns readable register data.
failureNotes: A missing ACK usually indicates the bus is not powered or the address is wrong.
Readable but invalid time data should be treated as present but unconfigured.

checks.description: Read a known RTC register to verify bus-level communication.
checks.passCriteria: The device acknowledges on I2C and returns readable register data.
failureNotes: A missing ACK usually indicates the bus is not powered or the address is wrong.
Readable but invalid time data should be treated as present but unconfigured.

notes: The shared I2C bus must already be initialized.
Any touch reset line must be released before probe.

checks.description: Confirm device touch is reachable through its declared I2C path.
checks.passCriteria: The controller responds on I2C and the interrupt line can be sampled.
failureNotes: A quiet interrupt line is not a fault by itself.
No I2C response usually indicates a power, reset, or address mismatch.

checks.description: Confirm the controller acknowledges on I2C.
checks.passCriteria: The controller responds on I2C and the interrupt line can be sampled.
failureNotes: A quiet interrupt line is not a fault by itself.
No I2C response usually indicates a power, reset, or address mismatch.

checks.description: Sample the interrupt line state without requiring a touch event.
checks.passCriteria: The controller responds on I2C and the interrupt line can be sampled.
failureNotes: A quiet interrupt line is not a fault by itself.
No I2C response usually indicates a power, reset, or address mismatch.

notes: The shared I2C bus must already be configured.
The board must expose a reset signal if hardware reset is required.

checks.description: Confirm device rfid is reachable through its declared I2C path.
checks.passCriteria: The part recovers from reset and responds on I2C.
failureNotes: A bad reset polarity can keep the device permanently offline.
Interrupt inactivity alone is not a failure if I2C probe succeeds.

checks.description: Assert and release reset if wired.
checks.passCriteria: The part recovers from reset and responds on I2C.
failureNotes: A bad reset polarity can keep the device permanently offline.
Interrupt inactivity alone is not a failure if I2C probe succeeds.

checks.description: Probe the configured I2C address.
checks.passCriteria: The part recovers from reset and responds on I2C.
failureNotes: A bad reset polarity can keep the device permanently offline.
Interrupt inactivity alone is not a failure if I2C probe succeeds.

checks.description: Read the board-mapped interrupt input for a stable idle state.
checks.passCriteria: The part recovers from reset and responds on I2C.
failureNotes: A bad reset polarity can keep the device permanently offline.
Interrupt inactivity alone is not a failure if I2C probe succeeds.

checks.description: Confirm bus display_spi is configured on the declared controller peripheral and signal lines.
checks.passCriteria: The bus can be opened using the declared controller peripheral and line mapping.

checks.description: Confirm the display_spi command path is usable before dependent device checks run.
checks.passCriteria: The SPI bus can drive chip-select and data lines for dependent devices.

notes: The display SPI bus must already be initialized.
Any board-local reset and backlight signals must be available if used.

checks.description: Confirm device display is reachable through its declared SPI path.
checks.passCriteria: The command path completes without transport error and any backlight control responds.
failureNotes: A passing command-path test does not guarantee pixel rendering is correct.
Shared reset wiring must be documented if the display reset line is multiplexed.

checks.description: Initialize the SPI peripheral for the panel bus.
checks.passCriteria: The command path completes without transport error and any backlight control responds.
failureNotes: A passing command-path test does not guarantee pixel rendering is correct.
Shared reset wiring must be documented if the display reset line is multiplexed.

checks.description: Transmit at least one known display command over the command path.
checks.passCriteria: The command path completes without transport error and any backlight control responds.
failureNotes: A passing command-path test does not guarantee pixel rendering is correct.
Shared reset wiring must be documented if the display reset line is multiplexed.

checks.description: Toggle backlight if that signal exists.
checks.passCriteria: The command path completes without transport error and any backlight control responds.
failureNotes: A passing command-path test does not guarantee pixel rendering is correct.
Shared reset wiring must be documented if the display reset line is multiplexed.

checks.description: Confirm signal lcd_backlight can be driven to the configured state for board bring-up.
checks.passCriteria: The signal can be driven to the requested board-level state.
